request: The categories across the top of the homepage are black and the contrast is bad. Put three lines top right with a dropdown of all the categories.

problem.contrast: The homepage header is transparent and sits on the hero photograph. Astra had the nav links at #2a2a2a - near black - over a navy scrim, and the scrim is a gradient that lightens to the right, so the last items were the worst.
problem.density: Twelve top-level items in a row, which was already flagged in the homepage audit as crowded.

solution: One navigation at every width: logo left, three-line toggle top right, one panel with all twelve items. Astra's own toggle, ARIA and JavaScript; only the appearance is ours.

the_two_traps.detail: With the Header Footer Builder active, astra_header_break_point() reads astra_get_tablet_breakpoint() and ignores the setting entirely. It was set to 3000 first, observed to have no effect, and then deliberately reset to empty so nobody reads a value there and believes it.

the_two_traps.trap: The astra_header_break_point filter alone is invisible
the_two_traps.detail: It moves the body class and the toggle JavaScript, but Astra also generates '@media (max-width:921.99px){#ast-desktop-header{display:none}}' and '@media (min-width:922px){#ast-mobile-header{display:none}}' into its inline CSS with the tablet breakpoint hardcoded. Without overriding those two rules the twelve-item row keeps rendering above 922px and nothing changes on screen.

why_the_filter_and_not_the_tablet_breakp: astra_get_tablet_breakpoint() feeds every responsive rule on the site. astra_header_break_point applies to the header alone, which is the whole intent.
risk_checked_first: The filter causes Astra to remove the 'ast-desktop' body class. Across the theme that class is used almost entirely for desktop submenu hover animations - 275 occurrences, the bulk of them in menu-animation CSS - which a burger menu does not have.

styling.toggle: 44px target, 4px radius. White with a hairline border over the transparent homepage header, navy elsewhere, keyed on the ast-theme-transparent-header body class.
styling.panel: White ground, navy links at 16px/600, hairline between items, ember on hover, ember rule on the current page, capped at the 1200px content column, scrolls if it outgrows the viewport.
styling.grouping: A heavier rule above Blog, where the shop links end and the rest of the site starts.

verification.page_types: Homepage, category archive, product page, guide and the problems hub all return 200, all carry the toggle and our CSS. Only the homepage is transparent, so only there is the toggle white.
verification.caveat: No screenshot - lookdog.club is unreachable from this environment. The open/close behaviour is Astra's own JavaScript, unchanged, but it is worth clicking the toggle once on a wide screen to confirm the panel opens where you expect.

second_pass.reported: Make the lines white, I don't see nothing inside, and put it 2.5cm lower

bugs.cause: Astra's transparent-header rule paints every .main-header-menu .menu-link white so the old inline row could sit on the hero photograph. The selector cannot distinguish a link in the header bar from a link inside the dropdown - it is the same menu - so on our white panel the items were white text. Present, clickable, invisible.
bugs.specificity: Astra's selector is five classes deep; ours was three. It won.
bugs.fix: !important on the panel link colour, its hover and the current-item colour. Our stylesheet also happens to print after Astra's, so the flag is belt and braces rather than the only thing holding it.

bugs.cause: .menu-toggle picks up Astra's global button rule - the same one that paints the orange pill buttons - and an ast-mobile-menu-trigger-outline treatment on top. The bars are an SVG using fill=currentColor, so whatever wins the colour cascade is the colour of the lines.
bugs.fix: !important colour and fill on the button and both SVGs, plus a semi-opaque navy plate behind them so the outline holds against a busy photograph.

adjustment.applied: padding-top:2.5cm on the primary header bar, scoped to the transparent header so only the homepage moves. Halved to 1.25cm under 640px, where 2.5cm is roughly a quarter of a phone screen.
adjustment.note: The logo and the toggle travel together, so they stay on one line.

verification.page_types: Homepage transparent and gets both the white toggle and the 2.5cm push. Category and product pages are not transparent, keep the navy toggle and keep their normal header position.
verification.source_order: Our override prints after Astra's white-link rule as well as carrying !important.
